basis: Acquired lanugo hair growth; glossitis affects 30-79%. Associated cancers are separate diseases; eyelid morphology alone does not establish ocular damage.
Peroxisome biogenesis disorder; neurologic impairment and cataracts or retinal degeneration affect most across the principal subtypes. Skeletal dysplasia is subtype-dependent.
Personality disorder without defining damage to any organ axis.
Progressive cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar atrophy and cognitive impairment; azoospermia and testicular atrophy are reproductive findings without established endocrine dysfunction.
Parainfluenza type 2 causes respiratory tract infection, particularly laryngotracheobronchitis.
Demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy with defining severe early scoliosis; scoliosis occurs in 11/18 and distal amyotrophy in 15/18. Hearing and ocular findings are occasional.
Defining loose anagen hair, congenital heart disease and frequent GH deficiency; hydrocephalus occurs in 30-79% with developmental delays. Skeletal findings omitted under the cap.
Lung parenchymal fibrosis caused by pulmonary tuberculosis.
Isolated foveal underdevelopment causes reduced visual acuity; no concomitant systemic pathology.
Airway ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis; recurrent infections are consequences rather than an intrinsic immune disorder.
Congenitally hypoplastic small intestine causes malabsorption. Reported cognitive and hair findings do not establish direct brain or skin damage rather than nutritional sequelae.
Defined by premature cranial suture fusion and displacement of the ocular lens.
Persistent inflammation of the larynx, usually from irritation, voice abuse or reflux; no inherent infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Malignant neoplasm involving the cerebral hemisphere; lymphoma is only one subtype of this umbrella.
XPR1-related primary brain calcification with neurologic dysfunction; localized cerebral calcification does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Zoonotic henipavirus infection whose principal organ manifestations are encephalitis and severe respiratory disease, including pneumonitis.
Congenital ichthyosis with erythroderma, hyperkeratosis and palmoplantar keratoderma; no established extracutaneous involvement.
PRPH2-related retinal pigment epithelial and macular dystrophy; visual acuity is reduced in 3/6 reported patients.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia with Joubert malformations; restrictive respiratory dysfunction/hypoplasia is a major asphyxiating feature. Retinal coloboma is 25%; renal frequency unestablished.
HTLV-1-associated immune-mediated inflammatory myeloneuropathy; bladder and bowel dysfunction reflect neural injury rather than direct urinary or intestinal damage.
Defining renal hamartomas/nephroblastomatosis and pancreatic islet hyperplasia with hyperinsulinism; developmental impairment affects 80-99%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
10q deletion umbrella commonly causes developmental delay and intellectual disability. Cardiac, renal and skeletal abnormalities vary with deletion extent and are not uniform across the group.
Squamous neoplasia arising on the ocular surface, principally conjunctival or corneal epithelium.
Bacterial infection umbrella covering Gardnerella and Bifidobacterium; no shared organ site across its constituent diseases.
TPK1 deficiency disrupts thiamine metabolism and causes childhood encephalopathy, dystonia and ataxia; lactic acidosis occurs in 3/5. Ventricular hypertrophy is only 1/5.
